newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Goldschmidt buy boosts Viag chemicals.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Goldschmidt buy boosts Viag chemicals.

text.p: German diversified utility Viag AG said on Monday it was buying chemicals group Th. Goldschmidt AG as part of its stated aim of strengthening its chemicals division.
Viag said it had agreed to buy a 27.95 percent stake in Goldschmidt from Ruetgers AG and 10.38 percent from insurer Allianz Versicherungs AG. Viag already owns 17.91 percent of Goldschmidt.

"The acquisition makes sense because Viag's previous holding in Goldschmidt was too small for Viag to make its influence felt," said utilities analyst Thomas Deser at BHF Bank in Frankfurt, adding that moves by Viag to expand its chemicals business were to be welcomed.
The companies have agreed not to disclose details of the transaction, including details of price, Viag and Ruetgers said in separate mandatory statements earlier in the day.
The acquisition has been rumoured for months and comes at a time of general consolidation in the international chemical industry.

With the industry's giants like Hoechst AG leading the way by spinning off unprofitable businesses and strengthening themselves with various acquisitions, analysts said smaller companies would likely face the future as part of larger conglomerates.
Analysts say global industry consolidation is just getting up to speed and many more changes will be forthcoming.
Viag said that after the completion of the purchase it would have a 56.24 percent stake in Goldschmidt and would control 50.34 percent of Goldschmidt's voting capital.
The transfer of the shares is still subject to approval by Germany's cartel authorities, Viag said.

Viag said Goldschmidt had opportunities to grow by cooperating with Viag's chemicals subsidiary SKW Trostberg although it had no plans to merge the two chemicals companies "in the foreseeable future".

Peter Antes, utilities analyst at Bayerische Vereinsbank in Munich, said: "The move is nothing new as we have known for quite some time that Viag wanted Goldschmidt, and we don't think it will have a dramatic effect on the share price and profit outlook."
Viag said it saw scope for cooperation particularly in the areas of silicone and tensides.
Since SKW's purchase of Master Builder Technologies last year, SKW is a world market leader for construction chemicals and has an extensive global sales network, Viag said.
In addition, "interesting prospects" opened up for Goldschmidt's tensides business, Viag said.

"It is a good fit for Viag. I think that it will be run within the Viag group structure initally, as SKW Trostberg is still bedding down other acquisitions and the chemicals sector is one of the core areas for Viag," said Antes.
Goldschmidt could be moved to within the Trostberg structure within three years.
"The aim of the majority takeover is to develop the company while retaining its own profile and to strengthen its strategic position on the world market," Viag said.
Viag's activities span the production of gas and electricity, packaging materials and chemicals as well as distribution and logistics.
